---
title: Authoring Markdown documents in Quarto 2
---

## Overview

Quarto 2 uses its own dialect of Markdown as its underlying document syntax.
Quarto's Markdown is largely based on Pandoc Markdown, itself an extended and slightly revised version of John Gruber's [Markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/) syntax.

Markdown is a plain text format that is designed to be easy to write, and, even more importantly, easy to read:

> A Markdown-formatted document should be publishable as-is, as plain text, without looking like it's been marked up with tags or formatting instructions. -- [John Gruber](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax#philosophy)

This document provides an introduction to Quarto's Markdown dialect (`qmd`).
Authors of Markdown will largely feel at home using `qmd` files.
The biggest conceptual change in Quarto 2 is that it can detect typos and syntax errors in your documents.
Unlike Markdown, some `qmd` files are not valid Quarto Markdown syntax and need to be fixed before your document will render.
For these situations, Quarto 2 offers an error message system with rich contextual information.

### Editorial marks

Editorial marks record suggested changes and comments in the document itself.
Each mark has an inline form, for a few words, and a block form, for whole paragraphs, lists or code.

The inline forms wrap text in brackets, with a two-character marker after the opening bracket:

```qmd
[++ inserted text], [-- deleted text],
[!! highlighted text] and [>> a comment].
```

[++ inserted text], [-- deleted text], [!! highlighted text] and [>> a comment].

The block forms put the same marker after the opening colons of a fenced div, and apply to everything up to the closing colons:

```qmd
::: --

This paragraph is marked as deleted.

So is this one.

:::
```

::: --

This paragraph is marked as deleted.

So is this one.

:::

`::: ++` marks inserted content, `::: !!` highlighted content, and `::: >>` a comment.
The marker must be followed by a space or the end of the line (`::: --draft` is an error, not a class).

Both forms take attributes, the inline form after the closing bracket and the block form after the marker.
By convention `author` and `date` record who made a change or comment, and when:

```qmd
Some text [>> needs a citation]{author="Ana" date="2026-09-24"}.

::: >> {author="Ana"}

A longer comment, over several paragraphs.

:::
```
